pairs.difference: A: the pan body is close to neutral grey and goes to flat charcoal in shadow, with no hue left under the rim or the underside. All the color sits in the cyan background, the red handle and the yolk. Shadow chroma kept is 0.22, far below the real range. B: the brass lamp keeps a gold-brown shadow color, and the glass picks up the green background. The hero and background hues are related, as on real cards.
pairs.fix: Give the dark pan a cool blue-violet tint in its shadows and a little cyan bounce light from the background on the rim, so the pan is not dead grey.

pairs.difference: A: the sneakers carry blue, lime green, teal, orange, magenta and yellow accents, on an orange and pale-yellow ground. That is about 5.5 hue families, above the real range, and the laces and sole are confetti-colored. B: the toaster is chrome tinted by the pink background, with one red knob as the accent and golden toast. That is three controlled families.
pairs.fix: Limit the sneakers to blue with one accent color. Use plain white laces and a white sole with no rainbow stripes.

pairs.difference: A: the shadow side of the cream jar turns green from the background (shadow chroma kept 1.78, well above the real range). The marble counter is a cool grey that does not belong with the green. The palette is only cream, red and green, about 2.6 families. B: the barrel's wood shadows deepen to a related red-brown. The steel hoops pick up sky cyan, and the warm deck against the cyan sky matches real cards.
pairs.fix: Shade the jar's dark side with a deeper warm cream-brown instead of green spill. Make the counter a light warm wood or a colored table rather than grey marble.

pairs.difference: B: the kettle is one pure, fully saturated red mass (subject chroma 0.17, above the real range), on a violet background with a black handle. There are under 2 hue families, and the shadow under the kettle is a desaturated purple (0.58 kept). A: the blue vending machine is loud too, but the multicolored cans inside break it up, and its shadows stay blue.
pairs.fix: Paint the kettle a slightly deeper cherry red with warm orange-red highlights and darker wine-red shadows. Add one small contrasting accent, such as a cream or teal knob on the lid.

pairs.difference: A: the whole card is pulled warm. The white tiles go cream-peach, the sunbeam upper left is yellow, and the background has almost no chroma (0.036), with a warm share of 0.95. The steel faucet is the only cool element. This is the same cream-instead-of-white shift seen in the generated computer lessons. B: the brick gate against a blue sky with green foliage has distinct hue roles and normal levels.
pairs.fix: Make the tiles a clean cool white or pale blue-grey and remove the yellow sunbeam. Put the faucet against a clearly colored wall, for example light teal tiles.

pairs.difference: A: almost the whole card is green. The background is green, and the whisk's steel wires reflect green, so the subject has almost no chroma of its own (0.05). The orange handle is the only warm area (warm share 0.017), giving under 2 hue families. B: the cream ferris wheel against blue sky, with yellow, red, blue and purple cabins, is a typical real color layout.
pairs.fix: Keep the whisk wires bright silver with cool blue-white highlights and draw the handle large and orange. Use a sunburst background in a hue that contrasts with the handle, for example blue or purple.

pairs.difference: A: the background is a neon, pure green (chroma 0.217, at the top of the real range), set against a hot pink-red popsicle. Both are at maximum loudness, with nothing neutral for the eye to rest on except the small stick. B: the orange wooden sign against sky blue with white clouds has a neutral rest area and keeps its wood color in the shadows.
pairs.fix: Make the green background a slightly deeper, less neon grass green with lighter sunburst rays. Give the popsicle soft white frost highlights so the pink is not saturated everywhere.

pairs.difference: A: the wooden table fills the frame in yellow-tan, and the glass plate turns yellow-green, so the card is mostly warm (warm share 0.85, at the top of the range). The fruit hues (red, orange, green, blue) are all at full chroma, louder than the muted background. B: the blue and white gingham gives a cool, neutral ground behind the warm board. Its hero/background split is clearer.
pairs.fix: Put the plate on a cool-colored tablecloth or a blue background instead of yellow wood. Make the glass plate clear with a pale blue tint.

pairs.difference: A: the white marble slab and its grey veins shift warm pink-beige in the lens. The dough and wood are tan, so the lower half becomes one warm beige mass under a purple backdrop. B: the cream scroll with a red ribbon and gold seal on a saturated blue table is a clear warm-on-cool split, as on real cards. Shadow chroma is similar on both.
pairs.fix: Keep the marble a cool white with blue-grey veins, or replace it with a colored countertop. Give the dough a warmer golden tone so it reads apart from the slab.

pairs.difference: A: the black stovetop goes brown-orange from the flame and the yellow tile wall, so even the darkest areas are warm (warm share 0.72, above the real range). Only the teal pot is cool, and the yellow wall competes with the hero. B: the orange and yellow feeder against green park foliage and a light sky has a cool rest area. The tree trunk shadows stay a related brown.
pairs.fix: Make the wall tiles a cool light blue or white and keep the stovetop a neutral dark grey with only a small orange glow under the flame.

pairs.difference: A: the mitts are a pure, uniform saturated orange with a red cuff, on a cyan-blue sunburst. This is the same orange-on-blue push as the generated baseball-glove lessons, with shadows that stay orange-red instead of going brown. B: the khaki jacket with a dark green sash and orange cuffs on green keeps believable local colors and muted neutrals.
pairs.fix: Make the mitts a slightly muted burnt orange or rust fabric, with darker brown-red shadows in the quilting and folds.

pairs.difference: A: four balloons in orange, red, teal and purple, plus orange strings, sit on a blue sky. That is about 5.5 hue families, above the real range, with every balloon at equal full chroma and no hero hue. B: the blue binocular viewer against a pale blue city with a soft peach horizon is restrained, with one hue family and a light warm accent.
pairs.fix: Use two or three balloons in one or two related colors, for example red and orange, against the blue sky, with white strings.

pattern: On color, generated cards are given away by: (1) the whole card pulled warm. Whites turn cream or peach, dark surfaces go brown, and grey marble or steel picks up a warm cast. (2) Local colors pushed to one pure hue, such as orange mitts, a red kettle or a neon green background, with shadows that stay the same hue instead of shifting to a related darker color. (3) The background tint leaking into the hero's shadows, or into the whole card so it reads almost one color. (4) Hue count off the real range: rainbow confetti accents (balloons, sneakers), or the opposite, a nearly single-hue card. Real cards keep cool neutral whites and greys, one clear hero-against-background hue split, and shadows that deepen toward related cooler colors.
